title: RL-SPH: Learning to Achieve Feasible Solutions for Integer Linear Programs
claim: Prior approaches need a solver or give only possibly feasible outputs; ours uses learning alone to directly yield feasible solutions.
layout: 3 stacked panels (a),(b),(c), left-to-right flows, shape-coded nodes with captions below
description: Three horizontal flow diagrams stacked in a compact layout. Panel (a), the top row and the longest, shows an existing E2EPH pipeline. A gray ILP instance box leads to a blue ML diamond, then a pink hexagon labeled partial solution, then a yellow ILP solver diamond, and finally a green feasible solution oval. Panel (b), bottom left, shows existing SPH. A gray ILP instance box leads to a purple non-ML diamond, then a dashed light-green oval labeled possibly feasible solution. Panel (c), bottom right, shows RL-SPH (ours). A gray ILP instance box leads to a blue ML diamond, then a solid green feasible solution oval. Node shapes and colors encode roles. The dashed outline marks uncertainty. Italic captions sit under each row. The eye goes first to the long top chain, then compares it with the short ours chain.
caption: Comparison among end-to-end learning-based primal heuristics (E2EPH), start primal heuristics (SPH), and ours.
abstract: Primal heuristics play a crucial role in quickly finding feasible solutions for NP-hard integer linear programming (ILP). Although $\textit{end-to-end learning}$-based primal heuristics (E2EPH) have recently been proposed, they are typically unable to independently generate feasible solutions. To address this challenge, we propose RL-SPH, a novel reinforcement learning-based start primal heuristic capable of independently generating feasible solutions, even for ILP involving non-binary integers. Empirically, RL-SPH rapidly obtains high-quality feasible solutions with a 100% feasibility rate, achieving on average a 28.6$\times$ lower primal gap and a 2.6$\times$ lower primal integral compared to existing start primal heuristics.
